Epstein's Temple & Secrets Decoded

The blue-and-white striped structure at the highest point of Jeffrey Epstein’s Little Saint James island has drawn sustained scrutiny as more than an architectural oddity. Constructed between 2010 and 2012 after local permits described only an octagonal music pavilion, the finished building carried a gold dome that echoed the Dome of the Rock before Hurricane Maria stripped it away in 2017. Document releases in late 2025 and throughout 2026 have shown the interior ceiling painted with zodiac figures, constellations, and mythical imagery, along with mattresses left on the floor, confirming that the space served purposes beyond any claimed music room.

Ghislaine Maxwell’s role places the structure inside a longer intelligence lineage. Her father Robert Maxwell maintained extensive documented ties to Israeli intelligence services, and Epstein’s calendars recorded dozens of meetings with former Prime Minister Ehud Barak after the 2008 conviction. The temple’s elevated location and distinctive design have been interpreted as a marker of that network, positioned where visitors could be observed or compromised with minimal external oversight.

🌍 Milan rally commemorates Iranian, Palestinian children killed in war

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Artists and demonstrators in Milan, Italy, have commemorated children killed in Iranian southern city of Minab and Gaza during events marking the 82nd anniversary of the Gorla school massacre in World War Two.

The commemorations took place in recent days as Italy marked the anniversary of the October 20, 1944, bombing of the Francesco Crispi elementary school in Milan’s Gorla district, in which 184 children and 19 school staff members were killed.
​
For the first time, Italy’s parliament this year recognized the anniversary as a national day of remembrance for children who are victims of war.
​
Participants drew parallels between the Gorla massacre, the killing of children at an elementary school in Minab, and the deaths of children in Gaza, paying tribute to the victims of all three tragedies.
​
Media activist Zio Filippo accompanied demonstrators from Piazza Repubblica to Piazza Venezia, using music videos to engage the public in the commemorations.
​
Italian artists also released a song titled “Gorla, Minab, Gaza” in memory of children killed in war.
​
Eighty-two years after the Gorla school bombing, the deaths of 157 Iranian schoolchildren in Minab during US-Israeli-imposed war against Iran have brought renewed attention to the killing of innocent children during armed conflicts.
